evidence.note: Mirrors jev-lint's validated built-ins ts-test-cannot-fail / swift-test-cannot-fail: holdout 12/12 per language, 0 false positives. Evidence that the wording works, not new evidence for this language.

Banik et al. (preprint, Jun 2026), 86,156 agent-authored test-file patches (Codex, Copilot, Devin, Cursor, Claude Code): 80.2% weak/no oracle; W1 no-assertion 24-85% by agent; W2 existence-only 0-0.4%; W4 mock-only 0-4%; W5 snapshot-only 0-4%.
Hora & Robbes, MSR 2026: 1.2M commits/2,168 TS/JS/Python repos; 23% of agent commits touch tests vs 13% human; 36% of agent commits add mocks vs 26% human.

kt-test-cannot-fail.whyNotLinter: detekt has no rule requiring a behaviour-dependent assertion; stub echoes and a mocked subject are semantic.
kt-test-cannot-fail.aiRelevance: Banik et al. find 80.2% of agent-authored test-file patches carry weak or no oracle signals (no-assertion is the largest class); Hora & Robbes find agents add mocks in 36% of commits vs 26% for humans.
kt-test-cannot-fail.notes: Refines best-practices/kotlin.md kt-test-cannot-fail: broader Kotest spec styles and runTest in the gate; MockK verify on unit-computed args made explicit.

evidence.note: kotlin.test assertFailsWith asserts that a block throws.

Banik et al. (preprint, Jun 2026), 86,156 agent-authored test-file patches (Codex, Copilot, Devin, Cursor, Claude Code): 80.2% weak/no oracle; W1 no-assertion 24-85% by agent; W2 existence-only 0-0.4%; W4 mock-only 0-4%; W5 snapshot-only 0-4%.

kt-test-error-path-passes-silently.whyNotLinter: detekt has no rule for expected-exception tests written with try/catch; intent must be read from the test.
kt-test-error-path-passes-silently.aiRelevance: Same agent failure mode as the Swift/Python variants.

evidence.note: With StandardTestDispatcher launched coroutines don't run until the scheduler advances; 'Always advance the scheduler before asserting on child coroutine effects'; runTest skips delay.
Luo et al., FSE 2014, 161 flaky-test fix commits: Async Wait 45% (34% use a fixed time delay; 54% fixed with waitFor), Concurrency 20%, Test Order Dependency 12% (74% fixed by cleaning shared state).

kt-test-launch-without-advance.whyNotLinter: detekt has no rule relating `launch` in tests to scheduler advancement; it depends on the dispatcher in use.
kt-test-launch-without-advance.aiRelevance: Agents migrating from `runBlocking` to `runTest` keep the old assertion order and get tests that pass or fail depending on dispatcher.
kt-test-launch-without-advance.expectedNoise: med — dispatcher setup is often outside the snippet; the rule is limited to launches visible in the test body.
